title: Material Disposal - Codroy NL
description: The work consists of the furnishing of all plant, labour, equipment and material for material disposal at Codroy, NL. In general, work under this contract will consist of, but will not necessarily be limited to, the following: 1. Removal of previously excavated/dredged material, which is currently stockpiled at the SCH main site in Codroy, NL. The disposal location for the soil is the DFO breakwater site northwest of the main facility. Note that the existing stockpile contains remnants of a plastic/enviroliner in amongst the soil. There may also be some wood and other debris in amongst the stockpile, from the previous dredging operations. In all cases, the plastics, wood, etc., are to be removed prior to disposing of the soil at the disposal site. Plastics/wood/etc., removed from the stockpile is to be transported off site and disposed of at a Provincially approved waste disposal facility. 2. Supply and installation of Class “B” and Class “A” granulars. 3. Supply and installation of 300mm diameter rock fill capping material to cover the soil at the disposal site. 4. Supply and installation of stone barricades at the approach to the disposal area.

title: RF Data Fusion for Command and Control
description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness levels (TRL) 1-9 can be submitted to this challenge. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/017 - RF Data Fusion for Command and Control The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) are seeking innovative software-based solutions to seamlessly convert, analyze, and fuse real-time, domain-specific, content-rich data transmitted over radio frequency (RF) bearers into a secure, standardized pan-domain Command and Control (C2) format to enhance interoperability and enable timely, data-driven decision-making across all domains and levels of command. Background and context Radio frequency (RF) communications in military operations are inherently bandwidth-constrained and vulnerable to jamming, interference, and environmental effects, making them unreliable in contested environments. To maintain timely and effective support across all warfighting domains, data transmitted over RF bearers should be transformed into compact, structured messages, such as eXtensible Markup Language (XML)-based Message Text Formats (MTF) or other machine-readable schemas. Such messages should be optimized for transmission over tactical networks including Low Frequency (LF), Very Low Frequency (VLF), High Frequency (HF), Ultra High Frequency (UHF), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM). This approach enables resilient, standards-based communication across domains (land, air, maritime, cyber, and space) and functional services (e.g., Joint Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (JISR), medical, logistics), in line with doctrinal requirements for pan-domain operations. CAF tactical messaging remains largely dependent on legacy systems. These systems are inflexible, poorly suited to machine-to-machine exchange, and increasingly misaligned with NATO’s shift toward XML-based, data-centric frameworks. CAF operators currently lack integrated, machine-readable messaging systems. As a result, they must manually convert voice, chat, and text inputs into formal military products including orders, situation reports, and Requests for Information (RFIs) to comply with command structures and coalition standards. Modern, pan-domain operations require that doctrinal and technical Information Exchange Requirements (IERs) be met at the speed of operational relevance, with messaging that is interoperable, standardized, and capable of supporting real-time, data-driven decision-making in joint and coalition environments. As NATO, the U.S. Department of Defense, and other Five Eyes partners adopt XML-based, machine-readable messaging frameworks, the CAF is prioritizing alignment with these emerging data models to improve interoperability, operational agility, and mission effectiveness. The DND/CAF are seeking innovative, interoperable, and scalable solutions that will contribute to the development of a next-generation digital military RF messaging and data exchange. Innovators are invited to propose technologies, platforms, or integrated systems. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Be a software-based capability (e.g., standalone application, plug-in, middleware, or service). • Support DND/CAF operations across all domains (land, air, maritime, space, cyber) and functional services (e.g., C2, intelligence, logistics). • Implement structured, standards-compliant messaging (e.g., MTF-XML) and data exchange protocols (e.g., National Information Exchange Model (NIEM), NATO Core Data Framework (NCDF)), with documented interfaces for importing, exporting, and exchanging data using those standards. • Be configurable and modular, supporting Character-Oriented Information Exchange (COIE) processing and designed for future extensibility (e.g., to accommodate emerging or disruptive standards). • Provide documented interfaces and standards-based data exchange mechanisms to support system integration, including use within experimentation, simulation, and wargaming environments. Desired Outcomes The proposed solution should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Operability in Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, and Low Bandwidth (DDIL) environments, with scalability to support evolving mission requirements and force structures. • Enhanced user experience features such as intuitive interfaces, multilingual support, automation of routine workflows, and built-in decision aids. • Standardized, documented integration interfaces (e.g., application programming interfaces (APIs)) to enable integration with at least one Service Management or Service Monitoring tools or platforms (e.g., ServiceNow, Splunk, Dynatrace, Microsoft System Center, Azure Monitor, etc.). • Readiness for future integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities to support data fusion, intelligent message prioritization, and real-time decision support.

title: RFI - WildFireSat Global
description: ***This Amendment is raised to extend the RFI end date to Thursday October 29, 2026 at 2:00PM (EDT)*** Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Where to find amendments to the tender document: The event messages tab and/or the event contents section in the SAP Business Network event. It is important you regularly check both. Where to submit questions about the tender document: The event messages tab of this event. Do not use the Q&A section appearing on the SAP Business Network Discovery website. Ensure you are fully registered in CanadaBuys/SAP Ariba! Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), on behalf of the Canadian Space Agency (CSA), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to solicit input from industry in support of the planning, definition, and implementation phases (i.e. Phases B, C and D)of the WildFireSat - Global (WFS). The WildFireSat - Global expands the original Canada-focused WildFireSat mission to a global scope for monitoring wildfire activity across 100% of the Earth’s vegetated land surface, while evaluating additional potential areas of interest, including Arctic and coastal regions. Canada will hold a virtual Industry Information Session on Tuesday June 2, 2026 at 11:00AM (EDT).

description: Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted by October 29, 2026 at 2:00pm EST. title: EP076-270289 Sir Frederick Banting Building Fire Alarm System Improvements
description: This project involves replacing the existing fire alarm system at the Sir Frederick Banting Building with a new fully addressable, networked fire alarm system while maintaining continuous building operations and fire protection throughout construction. The work includes installing new fire alarm equipment, devices, wiring, and controls; integrating the system with elevators, HVAC equipment, electromagnetic locks, fire protection systems, emergency generators, and the monitoring station; and completing all required testing, verification, commissioning, and code compliance activities. Once the new system is operational and accepted, the existing fire alarm infrastructure will be removed and all affected areas restored. The work will be carried out in phases within an occupied laboratory and office facility, requiring careful coordination to minimize disruptions and maintain life-safety functions at all times.

title: Keräyspaperin, tietoturvamateriaalin sekä SER-jätteen poistopalvelun hankinta
description: Keräyspaperin, tietoturvamateriaalin sekä SER-jätteen poistopalvelun hankinta Espoon kaupunki (myöhemmin myös Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia Keräyspaperin, tietoturvamateriaalin sekä SER-jätteen poistopalvelun hankintaan. Hankinnan kohteena oleva palvelu sisältää Espoon kaupungin sekä sen konserniyhtiöiden (Kiinteistö Oy Espoon Sotekiinteistöt, Kiinteistö Oy Espoon Keskuskeittiö, Kiinteistö Oy Espoon Koulu- ja päiväkotitilat, Espoon Asunnot Oy, Kiinteistö Oy Matinkylän uimahalli, Kiinteistö Oy Opinmäen Kampus, Weegee Oy ja Kiinteistö Oy Matinkylän Lukio) omistamien tai hallinnoimien rakennusten, tilojen ja toimipisteiden keräyspaperin, tietoturvamateriaalin sekä SER-jätteen poistopalvelut. Rakennukset sijaitsevat Espoon kaupungin alueella. Tilaajalla on myös muita sopimuksia, joita käytetään kuljetusominaisuuksiltaan vaaralliseksi jätteeksi luokiteltuun SER-jätteeseen sekä muun tietoturvamateriaalin poistopalvelussa. Suurin osa mm. perustietotekniikasta poistetaan tämän sopimuksen kautta. Tarjoaja voi toteuttaa osan palvelusta alihankintana. Tietoturvamateriaalin käsittelyä ja siihen liittyviä palveluita ei saa toteuttaa alihankintana, henkilöstövuokrauksella eikä muiden yksiköiden tai voimavarayksiköiden henkilöstöä käyttämällä. Palvelu tulee tuottaa kokonaisuudessaan tarjoajan omalla henkilöstöllä ja omana toimintana. Tarkempi kuvaus hankinnan sisällöstä on tarjouspyynnön liitteellä "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". Sopimus solmitaan yhden (1) Toimittajan kanssa. Lisäksi valitaan yksi (1) varatoimittaja. Sopimus on toistaiseksi voimassaoleva. Hankinnan ennakoitu kokonaisarvo on 717 000 (alv. 0 %). Eurot jakaantuvat hankintayksiköiden välillä seuraavasti: Espoon kaupunki 150 000€ Kiinteistö Oy Espoon Sotekiinteistöt 20 000€ Kiinteistö Oy Espoon Keskuskeittiö 10 000€ Kiinteistö Oy Espoon Koulu- ja päiväkotitilat 50 000€ Espoon Asunnot Oy 447 000€ Kiinteistö Oy Matinkylän uimahalli 10 000€ Kiinteistö Oy Opinmäen Kampus 10 000€ Weegee Oy 10 000€ Kiinteistö Oy Matinkylän Lukio 10 000€ Hankinnan valmistelu Hankintayksikkö on valmistellut hankintaa arvioimalla markkinoilla olevia vaihtoehtoja ja kilpailuolosuhteita sekä hankinnan toteuttamistapoja. Markkinakartoituksessa on kuultu alan toimijoita kirjallisesti, arvioitu hankinnan jakamista osiin sekä eri toteutusmalleja. Markkinakartoitus on toteutettu siten, ettei yksittäistä toimittajaa ole suosittu ja kartoituksessa on toimittu tasapuolisesti ja avoimesti. Hankinnan valmistelun yhteydessä toteutettiin markkinakartoitus potentiaalisista toimittajista tutustumalla hankinnan kohteena olevia palveluita tarjoavien toimittajien verkkosivuihin. Kartoituksessa tunnistettiin useita markkinoilla toimivia toimittajia. Hankintayksikkö lähestyi 8 toimittajaa lähettämällä 12.5.2026 tekniseen vuoropuheluun osan tarjouspyyntömateriaalista kommentoitavaksi sekä hankintaan liittyviä kysymyksiä vastattavaksi. Näistä kaksi yritystä vastasi kirjalliseen kommentointiin. Markkinavuoropuhelun tuloksia hyödynnettiin tarjouspyyntömateriaalin viimeistelyssä. Hankintayksikkö on arvioinut kirjallisen selvittelyn perusteella, että hankinnan kohteena oleville palveluille on olemassa toimivat markkinat ja että markkinoilla voi olla useita potentiaalisia toimittajia mutta kirjalliseen vuoropuheluun vastanneiden määrä jäi vähäiseksi. Kartoituksessa saatuja havaintoja hyödynnettiin hankinnan kohteen määrittelyssä, palvelutasovaatimusten arvioinnissa, hinnoittelurakenteen kehittämisessä sekä soveltuvuus- ja referenssivaatimusten tarkentamisessa. Hankinnan valmistelussa on huomioitu hankintalain 65 §:n mukaiset markkinakartoitusta koskevat periaatteet ja hankintayksikkö katsoo valmistelun tukevan kilpailun toteutumista. Hankinnan jakaminen osiin Hankintayksikkö on arvioinut hankinnan jakamista osiin. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, koska keräyspaperin, tietoturvamateriaalin ja SER-jätteen poistopalvelut muodostavat toiminnallisesti yhtenäisen palvelukokonaisuuden. Palveluiden tilaaminen, kohdehallinta, raportointi, laskutus ja Sopimuksen seuranta ovat samankaltaisia riippumatta poistettavasta jätejakeesta. Yhden toimittajan malli vähentää hallinnollista työtä, selkeyttää vastuunjakoa sekä tehostaa palvelun koordinointia Tilaajan laajassa ja hajautuneessa kohdeverkostossa. Hankintayksikkö katsoo, että jakamatta jättäminen on hankinnan luonne, toteutustapa ja tarkoituksenmukainen toteutus huomioon ottaen perusteltua.,

title: Finland – Locks, keys and hinges – Lukko- ja oviautomatiikkatarvikkeet ja palvelut OYS
description: Pohjois-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue Pohde pyytää tarjoustanne Lukko- ja oviautomatiikkatuotteista ja niihin liittyvistä palveluista. Hankinnan kohteena ovat lukituspalvelut Oulun Yliopistolliseen sairaalaan ja Peltolan kampukselle (Peltolan psykiatrian yksiköt sekä Konsti kehitysvammahuolto). Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, koska OYS:n ja Peltolan yksiköiden lukkopalvelut muodostavat toiminnallisesti, teknisesti ja turvallisuuden näkökulmasta yhtenäisen kokonaisuuden. Kohteiden lukitusjärjestelmät sekä ylläpito ja vikapalvelut edellyttävät keskitettyä kokonaisvastuuta. Hankinnan jakaminen usealle toimittajalle lisäisi rajapintoja, vastuunjakoa ja turvallisuusriskejä sekä vaikeuttaisi häiriötilanteiden hallintaa ja palvelun jatkuvuuden varmistamista. Lisäksi useamman toimittajan käyttö kasvattaisi hankintayksikön hallinnollista työtä ja voisi johtaa päällekkäisiin kustannuksiin. Tämän vuoksi hankinnan toteuttaminen yhtenä kokonaisuutena on palvelun laadun, turvallisuuden, toimintavarmuuden ja kokonaistaloudellisuuden kannalta perusteltua. Sopimuskausi on arviolta 1.2.2027 - 30.9.2028. Hankinnassa on kaksi mahdollista vuoden mittaista optiokautta. Hankinnan ennakoitu maksimiarvo on 1.700.000 € hankintakaudelle optiokaudet mukaan lukien laskettuna. Ennakoitu arvo on arvio perustuen historiatietoon. Uuden sairaalan rakennustyöt ja valmistuminen vaikuttavat tuleviin hankintamääriin. Tilaaja ei sitoudu annettuihin määriin vaan määrät voivat olla pienemmät tai suuremmat. Hankintasopimus ei muodosta Tilaajalle määräostovelvoitetta vaan tarvikkeita ja työtä hankintaan tarpeen mukaan. Hankinnassa valitaan yksi toimittaja. Päätöksen perusteena on suurimman kokonaispistemäärän saanut tarjous, joka täyttää pakottavat vaatimukset.

title: FCI Sheridan Water Loop Repair
description: FCI SHERIDAN WATER LOOP REPAIR Solicitation No. 15B61227Q00000001 Project No. 26Z6AV4 The Federal Bureau of Prisons, FCI Sheridan, requests firm-fixed-price quotations for repairs to the underground pre-insulated hot-water distribution loop at 27072 SW Ballston Road, Sheridan, Oregon 97378. This acquisition is a total small business set-aside. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, technical engineering, equipment, materials, and incidentals necessary to complete repairs at Locations A and B, including structural pipe lining, mechanical repairs, excavation, testing, and surface restoration. The SF 1449, amendments, and attached Statement of Work and Drawings establish the solicitation requirements. The Statement of Work and Drawings are incorporated into this solicitation and the resulting award. QUOTATION SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Submit the following: 1. Price Provide a firm-fixed-price quotation for CLIN 0001 covering the complete requirement, including security coordination, testing, restoration, warranties, and temporary hot-water contingency measures required by the SOW. Identify any assumptions or exceptions. 2. Technical Approach Submit a technical narrative not exceeding five pages addressing: � The repair approach and sequence for Locations A and B. � The proposed structural liner�s suitability for the specified temperatures and pressures, installation and curing procedures, and manufacturer warranty. � Excavation, welding, insulation restoration, leak-detection continuity, hydrostatic testing, and surface restoration. � The proposed completion schedule, including mobilization, personnel clearances, material availability, shutdowns, and testing. � How the work will satisfy the eight-consecutive-hour hot-water outage restriction per housing unit, including the temporary boiler contingency required by the SOW. � Coordination of escorts, tool control, utility isolation, and institutional work restrictions. Manufacturer technical data and warranty documentation are excluded from the five-page limit. Alternative products or components must include the technical documentation, certifications, and test results required by the SOW. 3. Relevant Experience Describe up to three comparable projects involving underground hot-water piping repairs or high-temperature structural pipe lining. Identify the scope, completion date, customer contact information, and whether the quoter performed as prime contractor or subcontractor. These descriptions are excluded from the technical approach page limit. ORAL PRESENTATIONS Each quoter submitting a timely quotation will participate in a virtual oral presentation of up to 30 minutes, including Government questions. The Government will provide scheduling instructions after quotation receipt. The proposed project manager or technical lead shall explain the repair approach, schedule, outage management, temporary hot-water contingency, and principal performance risks. Prepared slides are not required. The Government will evaluate information provided during the presentation together with the written quotation. Oral statements do not change solicitation requirements. Commitments relied upon for award shall be documented in writing and incorporated into the resulting contract. EVALUATION The Government will evaluate: 1. Technical approach. 2. Relevant experience and past performance. 3. Price. Technical approach and relevant experience and past performance, when combined, are more important than price. Technical approach will be evaluated for understanding of the requirement, feasibility of the repair sequence, suitability of proposed materials, and ability to meet technical, testing, security, restoration, schedule, and outage requirements. Relevant experience and past performance will be evaluated for similarity to the required work and demonstrated quality of performance. The Government may consider customer references, CPARS, and other available information, including performance as a subcontractor. A lack of relevant past performance information will receive a neutral assessment and will not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably. Price will be evaluated for completeness and fairness and reasonableness. CONFIDENCE RATINGS The Government will assign separate confidence ratings for technical approach and relevant experience and past performance, supported by documented findings: High Confidence: The Government has high confidence that the quoter understands the requirement, proposes a sound approach, and will successfully perform with little or no Government intervention. Some Confidence: The Government has some confidence in successful performance, but identified concerns may require Government intervention. Low Confidence: The Government has low confidence in successful performance, even with Government intervention. A neutral past performance assessment will not, by itself, increase or decrease confidence. STREAMLINED EVALUATION PROCESS The evaluation team will use on-the-spot consensus following review of each written quotation and oral presentation. The Government will document the findings supporting its conclusions. When multiple quotations are received, the Government may use comparative evaluation to assess their relative benefits and risks under the stated factors. The award decision will consider the underlying findings rather than ratings alone. BASIS FOR AWARD Award will be made to the responsible quoter whose quotation meets the solicitation requirements and provides the best value to the Government. The Government may select a higher-priced quotation when its evaluated benefits justify the additional price. If only one quotation is received, the Government will evaluate it against the stated requirements and factors and determine whether its price is fair and reasonable before award. The Government may communicate with quoters and request revised quotations as necessary. Quoters should submit their best initial quotation because award may be made without requesting revisions. SUBMISSION DEADLINE AND CONTACT Quotations are due October 29, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. Pacific Time, unless changed by a subsequent amendment. Submit quotations electronically to d1palmer@bop.gov. Identify solicitation number 15B61227Q00000001 in the subject line and acknowledge all solicitation amendments.

title: Chemical Nutrient Analysis Service for Combat Feeding Division (CFD)
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Natick Division, in support of the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC), Soldier Sustainment Directorate (SSD) / Combat Feeding Division (CFD) located in Natick, MA 01760, has a requirement for chemical nutrient analysis services for the U.S. Army Combat Feeding Division. The Combat Feeding Division�s Nutrient Analysis Laboratory (NAL) currently has multiple samples to analyze for nutritional content. The CFD, part of the U.S. Army DEVCOM-SC, is the Department of Defense�s centralized source for all research, development, engineering, and integration of joint service combat rations, food service equipment and field feeding systems. CFD�s primary mission is to ensure Warfighters have the tactical, nutritional and logistical advantage required to survive and win on the battlefield. Although CFD already has an in-house Nutrient Analysis Lab (NAL), there is currently a short-term need to outsource select nutrient analysis services for ingredients and ration components. The offeror shall provide laboratory nutrient analysis testing on provided food samples. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercially available services prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. Request For Proposal (RFP) number is: W911QY-26-R-NUTRIENT-ANALYSIS. The Government intends to issue a single award Indefinite Quantity Indefinite Delivery (IDIQ), Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract as a result of this solicitation. All timely offers will be considered, and proposal submission shall be in accordance with Submission Instructions contained herein. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability, Price, and Past Performance. Award will be made to the responsible vendor(s) that represents Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. The Government intends to evaluate submittals and award the contract without discussions. The Government reserves the right to conduct discussions if the Contracting Officer later determines them to be necessary. This requirement is for full and open competition. This requirement is not a small business set-aside. The NAICS code is 541380 - Testing Laboratories and Services. The small business size standard is $19,000,000.00. The Army�s Office for Small Business Programs concurs with the full and open competition determination. Incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular2026-01. (RFO) FAR Clauses 52.212-1 through 52.212-5, (see www.acquisition.gov) apply to this procurement. Offeror�s must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) to be eligible for award. Instructions for registration are available at the website. Any additional contract requirement(s) or terms and conditions determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary for this acquisition and consistent with customary commercial practices shall apply. Submission Instructions: All offerors shall submit a proposal consisting of two (2) sections. These two (2) sections shall be labeled; Section I � Technical Proposal; and Section II � Pricing Proposal. No Pricing Information shall be submitted in Section I. Evaluation will be in accordance with RFO FAR 52.212-2 Evaluation--Commercial Products and Commercial Services. (a) The Government intends to award a single award Indefinite Quantity Indefinite Delivery (IDIQ) contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to this solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: I. Technical capability of services offered to meet Government requirements: Requirements: The offeror shall be able to analyze samples for the analytes in Table 1 (See Attached Statement of Work for Table 1) with the preferred methods listed below or equivalent* with the listed limits of quantification (LOQ). The main analytes that will be requested are 1) selenium, 2) vitamin B12 (cobalamin) and 3) total dietary fiber. However, the offeror must also have the ability to analyze any of the other analytes listed in the SOW, CFD may need analysis of these analytes during the period of performance of this contract. This SOW is for an indeterminate quantity of samples. It is estimated that a minimum of 25 samples will be needed. The minimum guarantee for this contract is $5,000.00. The ceiling amount of this IDIQ contract is $25,000.00. No more than 25 samples are projected to be sent at one time. Analyses and results shall be completed and delivered to the government no later than 14 calendar days after receipt of samples. Offeror�s shall prepare a data report for each set of samples that has been analyzed to include sample name/ID, method used, results, units of measure, limit of quantification and date of analysis. *If the offeror proposes to use a different method than the preferred methods listed, than that method must be specified in their proposal as well as the LOQ of that method. If the method is not an industry standard method (publicly available), then please attach a copy of the method in the proposal. During market research, the price ranges in Table 2 (See Attached Statement of Work for Table 2) were determined to be reasonable per analyte (dependent on the method proposed). Offeror�s proposals must include the cost/test and the proposed method w/ LOQ. A cost/test can be outside of this range, but the proposals will be evaluated based on the demonstrated ability of the offeror to meet the requirements, proposed methods with LOQ and the cost/test. a. General Requirements In-House Capacity: The offeror must have the in-house capacity (personnel, equipment, etc.) to perform the analyses requested. Offerors acting as pass throughs to larger labs will not be accepted. Accreditation: The offeror shall maintain active ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for the duration of the contract. The accreditation scope must cover the specific nutritional tests requested. Analytical Methodology: All testing must utilize validated, industry-standard methods (e.g., AOAC International, USP, AACC, or equivalent recognized methods). If an alternative method is used, the offeror must provide scientific validation prior to testing. Sample Custody & Tracking: The offeror must maintain a documented chain of custody from sample receipt at the facility until final disposal. Communication & Support: The offeror shall designate a primary point of contact (POC) or project manager to handle inquiries, clarify test results, and resolve sample receipt issues within 24 hours. Storage Conditions: Upon receipt, the offeror shall store all samples under the conditions specified by the government (e.g., ambient, refrigerated at 4�C, or frozen at -20�C) to prevent nutrient degradation before analysis. Sample Retention: The offeror must retain the remaining homogenized sample material for a minimum of 30 calendar days after the final report is delivered, allowing the government to request re-testing if anomalies are found. Disposal: After the 30-day retention period, the offeror shall safely dispose of the food samples in accordance with local environmental regulations at no additional cost to the government. b. Specific Requirements See attached Statement of Work for Table 3 containing the Specific Requirements and additional details. II. Price: Reference Tables 1 & 2 in the attached SOW. Offerors shall fill-in the pricing information within the attached Pricing Spreadsheet titled �List of Samples - Nutrient Analysis� that contains the list of samples. title: USMCFP SPRINGFIELD - Bio-Medical Waste Removal
description: Completed SF1449 is required with bid and bid must be within spec of the Statement of Work to be considered. USMCFP SPRINGFIELD MEDICAL WASTE DISPOSAL: STATEMENT OF WORK Subject The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to make a single award to a responsible entity for the provision of Medical Waste Disposal for USMCFP Springfield. Medical Waste Disposal services shall only be used for medical hazardous waste that cannot be disposed of with garbage removed by the standard trash service. This contract is for Medical Waste Disposal that will need to be provided every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday throughout the contract. Place of Performance Services for Medical Waste Disposal will be performed at the address 1900 W Sunshine St. Springfield, Missouri 65807. There is a commercial entrance off Sunshine Steet to access the property. The driver will proceed to the talk box and receive directions from the officer. There is a small structure that houses medical waste. Period of Performance USMCFP Springfield is soliciting for a 12-month period of performance to start date of award and end 12 months after date of award with a 6-month option to extend to 18 months after date of original award. Schedule The contractor shall pick up Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays for the duration of the contract. Any deviation from this schedule will be mutually agreed upon by the Contractor and the Government. There will be no pickups on federal holidays. Pickups scheduled for federal holidays will be rescheduled for the next business day. Note: Three pickups will be required each week per policy. The time of pick up will be from 7:30 am to 10:30 am or 11:30 am to 2:30 pm. Licensing Requirements The institution requires all applicable Federal, EPA, and Missouri licensing / regulations that are standard for this industry. Service must also comply with the Disposal of Patient Materials standards which I have attached below: Security Clearance Services will be provided outside the secured confines of the institution. Please see the Terms and Conditions for any further requirements. Description of Duties The objective of this contract is to provide Medical Waste Disposal for USMCFP Springfield. The contractor shall be responsible for, but is not limited to, the following: The contractor shall be responsible for the collection, removal, and disposal of infectious medical waste. These duties must be in accordance with all Federal, State, City ordinances, laws, and regulations. Containers to furnish will be red, reusable plastic tubs with lid with overall dimensions of not to exceed (24x24x24 inches). Preferably 31 Gallon in size tubs. Tub liners and tape will be furnished by the contractor and appropriately supplied with each pickup. The contractor will leave an appropriate number of tubs and lids to exchange upon request. This includes providing properly sanitized tubs and lids. The contractor holder will determine an appropriate quantity of tubs to have on hand. On average 8 full tubs will be picked up Monday�s and Wednesday�s. Fridays will average 16-20 full tubs. The estimated medical waste to be removed is 85,000 lbs per year. Only the actual weight of waste collected will be billed. Disposal charge does not include the weight of the reusable tubs or lids. Electronic manifest is preferred Each Invoice will contain: Date of pickup, number of pickups, total weight of waste picked up, pricing according to the contract mirroring the line items on the contract. Point of Contact Contractor shall provide a Point of Contact (POC) who shall be responsible for the delivery of the services under this contract. The POC shall have the full authority to act on behalf of the contractor on all matters relating to the daily operation of the contracted services. The contractor shall designate this individual, in writing, to the Contracting Officer (CO) prior to contract start date. An alternate may be designated; however, the contractor must identify those times when the alternate shall be the primary POC. English Language Requirements The contractor performing the services under this contractual agreement shall have the ability to read, understand, fluently speak and legibly write in the English language. Government Quality Assurance The Government reserves the right to inspect and evaluate all services provided during the performance under this contract. All observations will be documented by the designated Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). When an observation indicates defective performance, the Contracting Officer, along with the support of the COR, may issue a Discrepancy Report to the contractor. The contractor shall address any Discrepancy Report in writing to the COR and the Contracting Officer, within ten (10) calendar days of notification indicating any corrective action to be taken to rectify the deficiency. Non-Personal Services Information The service is a contractual arrangement and not a personnel appointment. Payment is based on the provision of an end product or the accomplishment of a specific result. The service does not constitute an employer/employee relationship.

description: RFQ Amendment 0004 has been posted below. Furthermore, industry questions and answers are forthcoming based on the questions received from industry. NOTE: PLEASE BE ADVISED BEGINNING MONDAY, AUGUST 17, 2026 TRAVEL RESTIRICTIONS BEGIN AROUND THE RONALD REGAN BUILDING DUE TO THE PREPARATION FOR THE GRAND PRIX RACE. PLEASE ACCOUNT FOR POTENTIAL TRAVEL DELAY AND ALLOW ADDITONAL TRAVEL TIME TO ATTEND THE SITE VISIT SCHEDULED FOR MONDAY, AUGUST 17, 2026 AT 10AM ET. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Protective Service (FPS) has a requirement for corrective and preventative maintenance of electronic security systems and the replacement and removal of outdated electronic security systems at the Ronald Reagan Building (DC0459). The Contractor shall provide preventive maintenance, repair, replacement, lifecycle upgrades and installations to meet assessed security vulnerabilities / gaps in existing security systems. The services include, but are not limited to, routine and preventive maintenance, repairs and service calls. The VSS equipment includes, interior and exterior fixed IP cameras, controllers, monitors and NVR recorders, power supplies, and all associated ancillary equipment and infrastructure that are part of the Ronald Reagan Building Complex. The Period of Performance is for a one-year base ordering period with four one-year optional ordering periods. An Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with fixed priced provisions is anticipated. This acquisition is being solicited as a total Women-Owned Small Business set aside. Resultant task orders under this contract will be firm fixed price. The source selection process to be utilized for this acquisition is best value/trade-off. The technical, non-price factor, when combined, is more important than price. The submission requirements and evaluation criteria will be defined in the solicitation. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 561621 with size standard is $25 million. The successful Contractor is required to be register with the System for Award Management (SAM) at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for award. All questions must be submitted in writing to Contract Specialist Christopher Kelly at Christopher.Kelly@fps.dhs.gov.

title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

title: NAWCAD WOLF Tactical Voice Conferencing System (TVCS) Basic Ordering Agreement Task Order - 3
description: The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract to Cornet Technology, Inc. as a sole-source (other than full and open competition) Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) task order. This requirement is for the organic Lead Systems Integrator (oLSI) for the Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Webster Outlying Field (WOLF) operating under a product-based business model whereby NAWCAD WOLF civilians lead and manage the execution of the requirements with combined Government-Industry teams. Using this oLSI approach, the Government maintains control of intellectual property and data rights, enabling WOLF to rapidly adapt solutions to the dynamic needs of the warfighter. This requirement is for integration and installation, testing, site support, hardware and software maintenance, training, and hardware for the Tactical Voice Conferencing System (TVCS) OMNI system. The TVCS OMNI system, a replacement to the TVCS mid-range (MR) end-of-life system, is a Marine Corps Risk Management Framework (RMF) accredited communications, conferencing, and interconnect solution that provides radio and telephone conferencing functionality. The TVCS OMNI system fulfills a vital role in Command, Control, Communications, Military Air Management Control, and Mission Control. The function and purpose of the TVCS OMNI system is to provide Marine Corps Range Operators with secure and non-secure sea, air, and ground communications as well as the ability to communicate across networks with both secure and non-secure radios and telephones with carrier-class reliability. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole source basis under the statutory authority of Title 10, U.S.C. Section 3204(a) (1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. A determination by the Government not to compete this effort is solely within the discretion of the Government. description: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation FA8224-27-Q-0001 Portable Fire Extinguisher & Fire Suppression System Services For the benefit of AMXG, Hill AFB, UT This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA8224-27-Q-0001 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for monthly and annual inspection, maintenance, and monitoring of portable fire extinguishers, and annual fire suppression system inspection located within AMXG facilities at Hill AFB, Utah. As provided in the attached statement of work, all work on this contract shall comply with applicable federal, state, local, and Hill AFB fire prevention regulations It is the Government�s intention to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with a single entity for a one-year period with four additional option years. The Government is obligated only to the extent of authorized purchases actually made under the BPA by an authorized individual, and then only when performance of services has been made and accepted by the Government. All qualified sources are encouraged to submit a quote which will be considered by the agency. Contractors must provide proof of valid and active licensing issued by the Utah State Fire Marshal for servicing portable fire extinguishers as well as fire suppression systems. Contractor personnel must possess an active certification of registration by the Utah State Fire Marshal at time of service. Contractors must be registered at SAM.gov and have an active CAGE code at the time of response. A company that is not registered in SAM.gov or which does not possess an active CAGE code may contact APEX Accelerators for assistance in completing the registration process. A document with the APEX Accelerators contact information is included in this solicitation. Respondents to this solicitation shall specify whether the entity is a large business, 8(a) concern, women-owned small business, HUBZone small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business. Respondents must also specify whether they are a U.S.-owned or foreign-owned firm. This acquisition is 100% set-aside for small business concerns. To be considered a small business for this solicitation a company�s annual revenue may not exceed $25M. The NAICS Code for this solicitation is 561621. The provision at RFO 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services, applies to this acquisition. Quotations are due by Noon Mountain Daylight Saving Time on Friday, 30 October 2026 via electronic mail to ammon.helms@us.af.mil. Quoters are responsible for verifying receipt of Quote. Oral quotes will not be accepted. To be considered for award. Quoters are responsible for including the following eight items in their response: The solicitation number The name, address, telephone number of the Quoter A CAGE code and active SAM.gov Unique Entity ID. An active Portable Fire Extinguisher Company Privilege License Number issued by the Utah State Fire Marshal. An active Fire Suppression Systems Company Privilege License Number issued by the Utah State Fire Marshal. A company profile and capabilities statement that may not exceed one single-sided, letter-sized page. Completed FA8224-27-Q-0001 Pricing Response Form An affirmative statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms, conditions, and provisions included in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments. The provision at RFO 52.212-2, Evaluation � Commercial Products and Commercial Services Evaluation factors. The Government will award a contract (BPA) resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Offeror whose offer conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: Total Proposed Price, determined by the anticipated annual amounts of: 1,316 fire extinguisher inspections 7 fire suppression system inspections Estimated replacement of 20 10 lb. 2A:10B:C fire extinguishers. Technical Acceptability, determined by offeror�s quote meeting the requirements as outlined in the Statement of Work The clause at RFO 52.212-4, Terms and Conditions � Commercial Products and Commercial Services, applies to this acquisition The Government may make payment for BPA Call orders using a Government Purchase Card (GPC) or Wide Area Workflow Payment (WAWF). Notice to Quoters: The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse a quoter for any costs. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. title: Maintenance and Repairs of Aboveground Storage Tanks (AST) and Underground Storage Tanks (UST) at the Naval Station Newport; Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Newport Rhode Island and Other Areas of Responsibility (AOR)
description: This is not a request for either a quote or proposal, or an invitation for bid. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to notify potentials of a Facility Support, Firm Fixed Price (FFP)/Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Performance-Based contract with recurring and non-recurring services to perform Maintenance and Repairs of Aboveground Storage Tanks (AST) and Underground Storage Tanks (UST) at the Naval Station Newport Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Newport Rhode Island. General Work Requirements: Annex 1502000 - Facility Investment The contractor shall provide labor, management, supervision, tools, material and equipment, required to perform: Maintenance and Repair of Above Ground Storage Tanks (AST), Underground Storage Tanks (UST), leak detection systems, Emergency, Urgent and Routine (E/U/R) Work, Integrated Maintenance Program (IMP), AST/UST Inspection and Maintenance Program, and Hazardous Waste (HW) Disposal as described in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). The work identified is to be provided by means of a Facility Support, Firm Fixed Price (FFP)/Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with recurring and non-recurring services. Source Selection procedures will be used to select the proposal that provides the best Offeror using the Tradeoff analysis in accordance with FAR Part 15 � Source Selection Process. The solicitation and resulting contract award will be a performance-based service acquisition made to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to the Request for Proposals (RFP), will be advantageous to the Government price and other evaluation factors considered. The Offeror�s proposal shall contain a response to each of the evaluation factors and shall be in the form prescribed by the solicitation. The solicitation requires the evaluation of price and the following non-price factors: Factor 1 � Technical/ Approach Management Factor 2 � Corporate Experience Factor 3 � Safety Factor 4 � Past Performance. NOTE: The relative order of importance of the non-cost/price evaluation factors is; the technical factors (Factors 1, 2, and 3) are of equal importance to each other and, when combined, are equal in importance to the past performance evaluation/performance confidence assessment (Factor 4). When the proposal is evaluated as a whole, the technical factors and past performance/performance confidence assessment factor combined (i.e., the non-cost/price evaluation factors) are approximately equal to price. For Factor 2 Corporate Experience and Factor 4 Past Performance: The offeror shall submit projects that are similar in size, scope and complexity to the solicitation. Size: A contract with a yearly value of at least $200,000.00 for recurring services. Scope: Offeror must have provided all labor, management, supervision, tools, material, and equipment for Facility Investment Services for the Maintenance and Repairs of Aboveground Storage Tanks (AST) and Underground Storage Tanks (UST) as described in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Complexity: Offeror must have been responsible for responding simultaneously to requirements for several customers or installations. Offers shall be submitted for the performance of work for a period of one year. However, the initial term of the contract may be for a period of less than one year. The Government has the option to extend the term of the contract services for additional periods of one to twelve months. The contract will be for a base period with 4 (four) twelve-month option periods which, cumulatively, will not exceed sixty (60) months. The proposed procurement will be issued as a NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic Contract with online ordering capability using FedMall for the Non-Recurring Exhibit Line Item Numbers (ELINs). Acceptance of Government Purchase Credit Cards is required along with the purchase of FedMall Encrypted software. The North American Classification System (NAICS) for this procurement is 562998; the size standard is $16.5 million. The proposed procurement listed herein is a Competitive Full and Open/ Unrestricted procurement. The RFP will be made available in electronic format only (Adobe Acrobat (.pdf)) and will be posted on the SAM.gov website around 29 October 2026. The estimated proposal due date shall be at least 30 days after the RFP is posted. (Contractors - Technical inquiries must be submitted in writing to Asia Bracey, (asia.c.bracey.civ@us.navy.mil) 10 days prior to the RFP due date. The SAM site address is https://sam.gov . Notifications of any updates or amendments to the solicitation will be posted on the website only. Contractors are encouraged to register on the SAM website. Only registered contractors will be notified by e-mail when amendments to the solicitation are issued. IT IS THE SOLE RESPONISBILITY OF THE OFFEROR TO CONTINUALLY VIEW THE WEBSITE FOR CHANGES. All prospective contractors are required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. Failure to have an active registration in the SAM database at time of proposal submission will make an offeror ineligible for award. SAM registration shall be maintained until time of award, during performance and through final payment. Offerors and contractors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements via the Internet at https://sam.gov/. This contract will replace the contract for similar services. The current contract is N4008521D0015, Maintenance and Repair of Above Ground Storage Tanks (AST) and Underground Storage Tanks (UST) at Naval Station Newport, Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Newport, Rhode Island. The current contract expires 29 December 2026.

title: Head Start in State Systems Sole Source Award
description: This requirement was awarded through task order 47QRAA-20D-001M/7571MN26F80105 This requirement will support the generation and dissemination of research and/or evaluation that builds on the Financing Early Care and Education (ECE) Study task order (47QRAA-20D-001M/ 140D0422F0154). The primary objective is to generate and disseminate evidence pertaining to the financing of early care and education programs that meet child, family, and community needs. Building on data collected under the prior contract, this project will identify and elevate strategies used to align Head Start programs within state funding contexts to reduce administrative burden and expand the reach of ECE and Head Start funding. The research will focus on how Head Start programs operate within state systems and highlight effective strategies states have used to integrate or build upon Head Start funding within their broader early childhood systems. The project will also examine how efforts to streamline licensing and regulatory requirements, workforce standards, and supports for quality and technical assistance across funding streams can reduce burden, improve program efficiency, increase parental access to ECE, and support child and family outcomes. This requirement will build on prior efforts to identify and elevate financing approaches for states that most effectively align funding streams to both reduce burden and increase the reach of ECE funding. This project will provide ACF with critical evidence to understand how federal early care and education programs can achieve the Agency�s mission and vision of (1) supporting federalism & local leadership by providing actionable insights into how states and localities can leverage Head Start and other federal funding streams for early care and education (ECE) to best meet local needs, (2) promoting quality early learning environments and improved child outcomes by understanding how to leverage existing funding sources to best meet the preferences of families with young children consistent with their unique needs, and (3) promoting work and self-sufficiency by exploring how leveraging funds can expand the availability of ECE services that allow parents to work.

description: Pre-Solicitation Conference � NSWCPD Environmental Qualification Test Services The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) invites interested contractors to a pre-solicitation conference regarding the future requirement for Testing Services in support of Shock and Vibration and Electromagnetic Interference / Compatibility (EMI/EMC) Environmental Qualification efforts for Navy Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical (HME) equipment. This event is an opportunity for NSWCPD to inform industry partners about this upcoming need and to discuss potential strategies for meeting the demand. What: Pre-Solicitation Conference � NSWCPD Environmental Qualification Test Services When: 11/12/2026, 1230 - 1600 (In-person check-in: 1230-1300) Where: NSWCPD Philadelphia Navy Yard, Building 77L Room 200; 1000 Kitty Hawk Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19112. About Environmental Qualification Test Services: NSWCPD DEPARTMENT 30 conducts small to medium scale shock, vibration, and electromagnetic interference and electromagnetic compatibility (EMI/EMC) testing on shipboard and submarine hull, mechanical, and electrical (HME) equipment to reduce risks associated with new or updated equipment designs before they are installed on U.S. Navy ships. description: PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS NOTICE ONLY: THE SOLICITATION WILL BE AVAILABLE ON OR ABOUT OCTOBER 29, 2026 AT HTTPS://SAM.GOV/. Description: This acquisition may result in the award of a Design Bid Build (DBB) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Construction contract. for the renovation of a Maintenance Hangar at NAS JRB Fort Worth, Texas. The project consists of a two phased renovation of the interior and exterior of hangar 1050 including four separate interior admin spaces to better accommodate Marine Corps flight crews, equipment, and maintenance spaces for KC-130 and C-40 airframes. During renovation of Phase 1 spaces, aircraft maintenance operations will continue in Phase 2 areas. Similarly, when renovation continues into Phase 2 spaces, Phase 1 will be reoccupied and actively used for maintenance. Interior renovations encompass repair and replacement of all finishes, mechanical systems, plumbing, electrical, lighting, wet pipe fire suppression and fire alarm/mass notification systems. Exterior renovations include refinishing and repairing of the hangar doors and egress components and replacement of the hangar roof. Hangar bay renovation includes new electrical distribution, water distribution, waste water distribution, fire suppression, epoxy floor coating, compressed air system, heating and ventilation system and replacement of existing maintenance cranes and support railing. The contract performance period is 1,190 calendar days (inclusive of the base period and any exercised options) from the date of contract award. Schedule submission and progress tracking will be governed by FAR Clause 52.236-15, Schedules for Construction Contracts. The best value continuum source selection process to be used for this acquisition is the Tradeoff process in accordance with FAR 15.103-1. The Tradeoff process is appropriate when it may be in the best interest of the Government to consider award to other than the lowest priced offeror or other than the highest technically rated offeror. A sources sought notice was posted to sam.gov on July 1, 2026, requesting small business industry interested and capability statement. Based on responses from the notice it was determined that the requirement should be issued as Full and Open competition. The NAVFAC Small Business Office Concurs with this determination. The solicitation will be a negotiated DBB acquisition. Proposals will be solicited in a one-phase submission for a single solicitation. The solicitation will utilize source selection procedures, which require offerors to submit a technical proposal, past performance and experience information, and a price proposal for evaluation by the Government. Award will be made to the offeror whose total price and technical proposal offers the best value to the Government. Competition Requirements: Unrestricted basis, under full and open competition. Procurement Method: FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. Type of Contract: Firm-Fixed Price The NAICS code for this construction solicitation is 236220 with a size standard of $45,000,000. Project Magnitude is $90,000,000 or greater. This is a new procurement. It does not replace an existing contract. No prior contract information exists. A Site Visit will be held for those offerors who choose to participate (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). Proposals will be due no earlier than 30 days after the solicitation is released (exact date and time will be specified in the solicitation). This will be an electronic solicitation, which can be downloaded from Sam.gov Opportunities at https://sam.gov/. The solicitation will be available at this site no earlier than 15 days after this pre-solicitation notice is posted. Offerors are responsible for checking the Sam.gov website for the solicitation and any subsequent amendments that may be issued. description: This is a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) issued under the authority of DFARS 212.70. The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is focused on modernizing business operations by actively seeking innovative commercial technologies, products and services that will enhance our ability to deliver the military pay benefit at a significant patron savings. Authorized under DFARS Subpart 212-70, this CSO enables DeCA to competitively procure solutions through a streamlined acquisition process, allowing for rapid decisions. This approach underscores our mission to expedite the award and delivery of critical technologies, products, and services, ensuring that DeCA can leverage advancements in the grocery resale industry swiftly and efficiently. By prioritizing speed in our contracting efforts, we aim to support the timely integration of cutting-edge technologies, products, and services that enhance our ability to: improve the commissary benefit; decrease costs without diminishing the benefit; improve processes that have a high risk of potential fraud, waste, or abuse; and reduce waste and decrease variation in processes. Through this initiative, DeCA reaffirms its commitment to fostering innovation and enhancing business operations, ultimately delivering a vital benefit of the military compensation package that improves quality of life and readiness by providing grocery items at significant savings.

Reserves will be allocated for 8(a), HUBZone, Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB), and Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB). More detailed information regarding the Reserves is included in the solicitation document. PSC Code: Z2AA NAICS Code: 236220 Small Business Size Standard: $45M Description: This is a Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract that provides for an indefinite quantity of supplies or services during a fixed period. The GSA intends to award multiple contracts for General Construction Services. After award of the IDIQ all awardees will be provided fair opportunity in accordance with FAR 16.507-2 for discrete construction projects where a single task order will be issued based on selection criteria established at the ordering level, unless an exemption exists in accordance with FAR 16.507-6. The General Contractor (GC) shall serve as the single point of responsibility and must supervise, administer, coordinate, perform, and contract all management, labor, materials, equipment, and construction activities required to successfully execute each assigned project. Construction services will be required to be performed at federally owned and leased locations. The operational scope encompasses comprehensive general construction, repair, alteration, and modernization services for existing real property facilities. The General Contractor (GC) shall supervise, administer, perform, and contract all construction activities required to complete a project. Construction services include, but are not limited to office construction and/or renovations/repairs, office space renovations, MEP (Mechanical/Electrical/Plumbing) repairs/modifications/replacement, fire sprinkler systems repairs/modification/replacement, sitework, exterior construction repair and alterations (including facades and roofs), demolition (including abatement of hazardous materials), elevator modernizations, work in technically sensitive environments like laboratories, SCIF�s etc., work in high-security data centers and critical infrastructure control systems, construction work in high security buildings, as well as any other general construction activities. The scope will include design-build services. The GC may be required to utilize the following delivery methods to deliver projects for the GSA: 1. Design/Bid/Build (DBB) Traditional 2. Design/Build (D/B) The primary geography will cover: -All of Washington, D.C. -Virginia: Arlington County, Fairfax County, Loudon County, Independent Cities of Alexandria, Fairfax, and Falls Church -Maryland: Montgomery County, Prince George's County The Government may unilaterally expand the geography to cover any additional counties in the states of Maryland and Virginia. GSA reserves the right to expand, within scope, the geographic areas covered by the awarded contracts by bilateral agreement with any or all contract holders based on agency needs and requirements. The Maximum Ordering Limit (MOL) for this contract vehicle is $500,000,000.00. Meaning the cumulative total for all task orders awarded to all contractors over the life of the contract (5 Years) is not anticipated to exceed $500,000,000.00. There is no MOL per contractor or per performance period. The general task order range will be between $350,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. There will be a base period of one (1) year, and there will be four (4) option periods of one-year each, for a total possible performance period of five (5) years. The government intends to award approximately eighteen (18) contracts, inclusive of a target of twelve (12) contract reserves. However, the Government reserves the right to make more, fewer, or no awards, depending on the results of the evaluation, availability of funding, and the Government�s needs. The government is reserving three (3) contracts each for the following socioeconomic designations: 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB, for a target of twelve (12) contract reserves. However, the Government reserves the right to make more, fewer, or no reserve awards, depending on the results of the evaluation, availability of funding, and the Government�s needs. Award Methodology This solicitation will be executed pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.103-3 (RFO-2025-15), Highest technically rated with a fair and reasonable price approach. Pursuant to FAR Clause 52.215-1 Instructions to Offerors-Competitive Acquisition, and FAR 15.203 (RFO-2025-15), the Government intends to evaluate proposals and make competitive awards without negotiations with offerors although it reserves the right to negotiate should it be determined to be necessary. Competitive proposals shall be evaluated and assessed based on the factors specified in this solicitation. For this solicitation, all evaluation factors other than cost or price, when combined, are significantly more important than price. The Technical Evaluation Factors will be: Prior Experience Past Performance Evidence of Bonding Capacity: Go/No Go. (Minimum- $10M per project) Prior Experience is relatively more important than Past Performance. More detailed information regarding the technical factors and award methodology is included in the solicitation. Awards are anticipated to be made in February of 2027. The proposed contract is other than full and option competition (Attached Justification and Approval (J&A) will be provided). Applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 238210 and has a size standard of $19 Million. Offerors are required to provide FOB Destination pricing to NUWC Keyport, WA 98345-7610. Requirements and evaluation procedures are listed in the attached solicitation, which is required to be filled out in its entirety and returned before the solicitation closes. All questions regarding this solicitation should be submitted in writing as soon as practicable after receipt of solicitation. title: Gardening services for The US embassy in Bogot�, Colombia
description: The requirement is for providing Gardening Services for properties owned or managed by the United States Government as official office and operational space for the Mission in Bogot�, Colombia. The Contractor shall provide comprehensive gardening and landscape maintenance services for the U.S. Embassy Bogota compound. These services shall include all planning, administration, and management necessary to ensure compliance with the contract, the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) schedules and instructions, and all applicable best practices, laws, and regulations. The Contractor must meet all performance standards specified in the contract. The Contractor shall also perform all related support functions, including but not limited to human resources management, quality control, technical oversight, and phytosanitary supervision. The green areas of the U.S. Embassy Bogota compound cover approximately 28,000 square meters, as highlighted in the reference image below. Areas requiring gardening services include lawns, trees, palms, shrubs, hedges, bushes, vines, ground cover, flower beds, and selected indoor plants. In addition, the scope of services includes all roofs and hard surfaces where activities must be performed, as described in this Statement of Work (SOW). The scope also includes the immediate exterior perimeter, primarily planters and exterior gardens at the entrances to the Embassy compound. The anticipated performance period is for a base year, with four one-year option periods, and a possibility of 6 months extension if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered. The Contractor shall verify these conditions during the site walkthrough as part of the Request for Proposal (RFP) process The Government may award the contract based on the initial offer without discussion. The resultant contract will be a firm fixed price type contract. Notwithstanding FAR 4.203 - 1(b)(5)(ii), the Contracting Officer has determined that it is in the best interest of the U.S. Government that offerors be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) database at https://www.sam.gov at the time of submitting a proposal. title: Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility Services AE IDIQ, Unrestricted
description: THIS IS AN UNRESTRICTED PROCUREMENT. This procurement will result in one Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for multi-discipline Architect-Engineer (A-E) services for Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility services at various Navy and Marine Corps installations primarily in the Navy Region Southwest but may also include work worldwide. These services will be procured in accordance with 40 USC Chapter 11, Selection of Architects and Engineers, as implemented by FAR 36. The IDIQ contract will be for a base period of two (2) years and three (3) one-year option periods (if exercised). The total fee for the contract term shall not exceed $30,000,000. The guaranteed minimum for the contract term (including option years) is $1,000. Firm-fixed price task orders will be negotiated for this contract. The minimum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $25,000. The maximum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $2,500,000. There will be no dollar limit per year. Estimated start date is March 2027. The Small Business size standard classification is North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330 (Engineering Services). The Government seeks the most highly qualified firm to perform the required services, based on the demonstrated competence and qualifications, in accordance with the selection criteria. Primary A-E Services: 1. Land Use Planning. 2. Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (AICUZ) and Range Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (RAICUZ) Studies. 3. Encroachment Action Plans (EAP) or Encroachment Control Plans (ECP). 4. Strategic Engagement and Communication Plans (SECP). 5. Outreach Planning Materials. 6. Electronic Database. Secondary Services: 1. Other related studies/analysis: Provide additional services to assist in implementation of encroachment management studies, Range Complex Management Plans (RCMP), Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMP), Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration (REPI) Program plans, and other special planning, engineering, and encroachment support deliverables, such as analytical assessments, geospatial analysis and simulations, traffic studies, glint/glare analysis, radar assessments, plume analysis and modeling, lighting studies, and socio-economic studies. 2. Other Related Reports or Documentation: Deliverables also include assistance with incidental services related to providing public notice for studies and publicizing and providing training on encroachment-related studies. Please see attached synopsis for full synopsis description/instructions.
